name: Bongard-LOGO
ability_definition: The ability to generate or use different sets of rules for combining or grouping things in different ways.

task_realism.reasoning: Each problem asks the system to infer which abstract rule separates six synthetic LOGO-drawn stroke figures from six others. Real workplace uses of category flexibility look different: re-sorting inventory, customers, documents, cases or data records under shifting criteria, often with meaningful semantic attributes. The cognitive core does exist here, namely rule induction and context-dependent reinterpretation of the same stroke (zigzag as a line versus triangles). But the task content is a perceptual puzzle with no workplace analog.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Conditions are clean, few-shot and closed-world. Stimuli are noise-free and noted as balanced, time is unlimited, and nothing is at stake. There is no ambiguity about whether a rule exists, and no need to decide which grouping is useful for a goal. Real work involves messy, multi-attribute inputs, stakeholder-defined purposes and incomplete information. The held-out splits (novel abstract, combinatorial) do test generalization to unseen rules, which adds some realism.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark covers the 'use a rule' side of the ability well. Each problem needs a new rule, and context-dependent perception tests whether the same features can be grouped differently. It misses the 'generate multiple rule sets' side: each problem is a single binary partition, and the system never regroups a fixed item set itself or produces alternative groupings. It is also restricted to visual shape attributes, excluding semantic, numerical and verbal categorization.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are black-and-white synthetic stroke drawings, and the output is a forced binary classification of a query image. Workplace artifacts for grouping tasks are spreadsheets, records, product lists, text or real images. Outputs there are category schemes, labels or reorganized structures, not a single yes/no on a toy figure.

transferability_reasoning: Bongard-LOGO isolates a genuine component of category flexibility: inducing a new grouping rule from few examples, and reinterpreting features depending on context. It does so in a highly artificial visual puzzle format with binary outputs. It does not require generating or switching among multiple groupings of the same items, and its synthetic stimuli and clean conditions bear little resemblance to workplace categorization. Strong performance would therefore only weakly predict real-world regrouping capability.

2021.metric: test accuracy (%) on the free-form shape (FF) test split; chance = 50
2021.human_reference: General educated adults doing few-shot visual concept induction. These are non-expert solvers, comparable to the 'Human (Amateur)' baseline in Nie et al.
